18	### Planted training quirk discovered while setting up
19	Passing **`-maxn 0` explicitly** aborts training deterministically:
20	
21	```
22	terminate called after throwing an instance of 'fasttext::DenseMatrix::EncounteredNaNError'
23	  what():  Encountered NaN.
24	```
25	exit code **134** (SIGABRT, core dumped), no model saved. Trigger conditions verified:
26	- `-minn 0 -maxn 0` → abort
27	- `-maxn 0` alone → abort
28	- `-minn 0` alone → OK
29	- omitting both flags (defaults are also 0/0) → OK (!)
30	- `-minn 0 -maxn 4`, `-minn 2 -maxn 2` → OK
31	So the abort is triggered by the flag being *explicitly present with value 0*, not by the value itself.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## Common formatting facts
36	
37	- All float output uses C++ `std::ostream` default formatting: **6 significant digits**, no trailing zeros, switches to scientific notation for extreme magnitudes (`5.1025e+36`, `4.271e-41`), prints `-nan` for NaN.
38	- Vector lines (word/sentence/ngram) end with a **trailing space before the newline**: `... -0.058374 \n` (confirmed with `od -c`).
39	- Neighbor lines (`nn`/`analogies`) are `word SP score \n` with **no** trailing space.
40	- Usage messages go to **stdout**, exit code **1**, e.g.:
41	
42	```
43	usage: fasttext nn <model> <k>
44	
45	  <model>      model filename
46	  <k>          (optional; 10 by default) predict top k labels
47	
48	```
49	(note the trailing blank line). Same shape for `analogies`, `print-ngrams`, `print-word-vectors`, `print-sentence-vectors`.
50	- Missing/unopenable model file → abort on **stderr**, exit **134**:
51	```
52	terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
53	  what():  nosuch.bin cannot be opened for loading!
54	```
55	
56	---
57	
58	## 1. `print-word-vectors <model>`
59	
60	Reads **whitespace-separated tokens** from stdin (space/tab/CR/LF all delimit), prints one line per token: `word SP v1 SP ... SP vdim SP \n`.
61	
62	Command: `printf 'king\nqueen\n' | /workspace/executable print-word-vectors sg.bin | cat -A`
63	
64	```
65	king -0.13976 0.1898 -0.10719 -0.0073993 0.052704 0.079712 0.11318 -0.058374 $
66	queen -0.11813 0.17171 -0.097323 -0.014527 0.045492 0.080585 0.099487 -0.056853 $
67	```
68	
69	Verified behaviors (exit always 0):
70	- Multiple words per line → one output line per word (same as one-per-line).
71	- Leading/trailing spaces, tabs, `\r\n` line endings → silently treated as delimiters; `king\r\n` prints the plain `king` vector.
72	- Blank lines / whitespace-only lines → **no output at all**.
73	- EOF without trailing newline → last token still processed; empty stdin → no output, exit 0.
74	- Case/punctuation are NOT normalized: `King`, `king,`, `king.`, `KING` are distinct (OOV) tokens with distinct vectors.
75	- OOV with subword model (`sg.bin`, `cb.bin`): non-zero vector computed from subword ngrams, e.g. `zzqwxv 0.0002495 -0.0034874 0.0014513 0.0043441 -0.012947 0.0025509 0.0045073 0.0052475`.
76	- **Quirk — OOV with the no-subword model (`sgnosub.bin`)**: still returns a **non-zero, deterministic** vector (upstream fastText returns all zeros here):
77	```
78	zzqwxv -0.029706 0.031074 -0.022902 0.0044358 0.012054 0.0071257 0.016799 -0.011826 
79	abcqqz -0.050183 0.048313 -0.034369 0.0090521 0.017715 0.0085209 0.027264 -0.013891 
80	```
81	  Same across repeated runs and repeated queries; does not match any in-vocab word vector or the vocab mean (checked numerically against `sgnosub.vec`). Appears hash-derived from the token string.
82	
83	## 2. `print-sentence-vectors <model>`
84	
85	Reads **line-wise** (one output line per input line). Sentence vector = L2-normalized mean of the token word vectors (verified numerically: norm ≈ 1.0, matches normalized average of `print-word-vectors` output up to print rounding). Format: `v1 SP ... SP vdim SP \n` (no leading word, trailing space).
86	
87	Command: `printf 'king queen\nking\n\nzzqwxv\n' | /workspace/executable print-sentence-vectors sg.bin | cat -A`
88	
89	```
90	-0.44576 0.62599 -0.35418 -0.038724 0.16983 0.27839 0.36799 -0.19992 $   <- "king queen"
91	-0.45964 0.62422 -0.35255 -0.024335 0.17334 0.26216 0.37225 -0.19198 $   <- "king" (= normalized word vec)
92	0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 $                                                        <- EMPTY line -> exact zeros
93	0.015619 -0.21831 0.090851 0.27194 -0.81048 0.15969 0.28216 0.32849 $   <- OOV-only "zzqwxv" (subwords)
94	```
95	
96	- Empty line and whitespace-only line → `0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 ` (trailing space kept).
97	- OOV tokens DO affect the average (`king zzqwxv` ≠ `king`); with subwords via ngrams, without subwords via the pseudo-vector quirk above (OOV-only sentence on `sgnosub.bin` is also non-zero).
98	- EOF without newline → last line processed. Exit 0.
99	
100	## 3. `print-ngrams <model> <word>`  — heavily quirky
101	
102	Usage error (wrong arg count) → usage to stdout, exit 1.
103	
104	Format: one line per subword: `subword SP v1 SP ... SP vdim SP \n`. Subword **strings** are correct and deterministic: computed on the `<word>`-wrapped token, ordered by start position, then increasing ngram length (minn..maxn). For an **in-vocab** word a first extra line `word SP <vec>` is printed (12 subword lines for `king` with minn=2/maxn=4: `<k <ki <kin ki kin king in ing ing> ng ng> g>`); for an **OOV** word there is no leading word line (18 lines for `zzqwxv`).
105	
106	**Quirk A — vectors are garbage/uninitialized memory.** The numeric columns contain huge/denormal/NaN values and are **non-deterministic across runs**. Two consecutive runs of `/workspace/executable print-ngrams sg.bin king`, first line:
107	
108	```
109	king -7.6096e+34 0.19353 -7.6096e+34 0.05991 0.049921 -0.0011264 0.1267 -0.016408 
110	king -1.4914e+26 0.19353 -1.4914e+26 0.05991 0.049921 -0.0011264 0.1267 -0.016408 
111	```
112	
113	Sample (single run, `cat -A`):
114	
115	```
116	king 5.1025e+36 0.19353 5.1025e+36 0.05991 0.049921 -0.0011264 0.1267 -0.016408 $
117	<k -0.11426 -nan -0.095416 -3.4608e+12 -1.682e+31 1.8954e+38 0.093193 -0.0513 $
118	```
119	
120	Notes:
121	- Some slots vary per run (`5.1025e+36` vs `-7.6096e+34` vs `-1.4914e+26` in the same position), others are stable constants that even recur across *different* models (`9.9446e+07`, `48583`, `-1.2692e+10`, `2.7981e+22`, `1.2265e+35`, `6068.x`, `-93.4xx`, `-nan`).
122	- Some lines are all zeros; some lines repeat the same plausible-looking vector many times (e.g. `-0.11426 0.15733 -0.095416 -0.010786 0.043826 0.071584 0.093193 -0.0513` on `sg.bin`), but even those do not match the word's `print-word-vectors` output. Nothing printed here can be trusted as a real vector.
123	- Same behavior on `cb.bin`.
124	
125	**Quirk B — no-subword model.** `print-ngrams sgnosub.bin king` still prints 10 subword lines, and they are **length 3..6 ngrams** (`<ki <kin <king <king> kin king king> ing ing> ng>`) — i.e. when maxn=0 it falls back to fastText's *default* minn=3/maxn=6 range instead of printing nothing. Vectors are garbage as above (plus some all-zero lines). OOV word on this model: same 3..6 behavior.
126	
127	Edge cases: empty-string word (`print-ngrams sg.bin ''`) prints one line `<> <garbage vec>`; exit code always 0.
128	
129	## 4. `nn <model> [k]` — interactive
130	
131	- Reads **whitespace-separated tokens** (`operator>>`-style): blank lines are skipped, a line `king queen` produces TWO consecutive queries. Exit on EOF, code 0.
132	- Prompt goes to **stdout**: exactly `Query word? ` (trailing space, no newline); results start on the same line. At EOF a final `Query word? ` is printed with **no trailing newline** (od-verified: file ends `Q u e r y   w o r d ?  `).
133	- Unlike `analogies`, `nn` prints **no** "Loading model" line.
134	- Output per neighbor: `word SP score\n`, score = cosine similarity, 6 sig figs. Query word itself excluded. `</s>` can appear as a neighbor.
135	- Default k=10. Results deterministic across runs.
136	
137	`printf 'king\n' | /workspace/executable nn sg.bin 3 | cat -A`:
138	
139	```
140	Query word? banana 0.99889$
141	slow 0.998731$
142	big 0.998721$
143	Query word? 
144	```
145	
146	k handling (asymmetric with `analogies` — quirk):
147	- `nn sg.bin 0` → accepted, prints prompt, **zero** result lines, exit 0.
148	- `nn sg.bin -1` (any negative) → prints **the entire dictionary minus the query word** (22 lines for this 23-word vocab), exit 0.
149	- `nn sg.bin abc` → abort, exit 134:
150	```
151	terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
152	  what():  stoi
153	```
154	- OOV query works on all models (subword vector, or the pseudo-vector quirk on `sgnosub.bin` — it still returns plausible neighbors, e.g. `house 0.999519 ...`), scores can be negative (`walk -0.185405`).
155	
156	## 5. `analogies <model> [k]` — interactive, contains a severe quirk
157	
158	- First stdout line (absent in `nn`): `Loading model sg.bin\n` (echoes the model path as given).
159	- Prompt on stdout, exactly `Query triplet (A - B + C)? ` (trailing space); results begin on the same line: `word SP score\n`.
160	- Reads three whitespace-separated tokens per query (blank lines skipped; tokens may span lines). A, B and C are **excluded** from results (k=25 returns only 20 lines for a 23-word vocab).
161	- Default k=10; works identically on `sg.bin` and `cb.bin`.
162	- k validation: `analogies sg.bin 0` or `-1` → abort, exit 134:
163	```
164	terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
165	  what():  k needs to be 1 or higher!
166	```
167	`analogies sg.bin abc` → `what():  stoi` abort, exit 134. (Contrast: `nn` accepts k<=0 silently.)
168	- OOV tokens in the triplet are accepted (subword/pseudo-vector quirk).
169	
170	**Quirk — infinite loop at EOF.** When stdin reaches EOF, `analogies` does NOT exit; it reprints `Query triplet (A - B + C)? ` followed by the **same results as the previous query**, forever (~120k–240k iterations in 2 s, tens of MB of output). Even a *partial* triplet (`man king\n` then EOF) is answered (with low near-zero scores — the missing third word behaves as an empty/zero token) and then loops forever. Only way out is SIGKILL/SIGINT/timeout; it never exits by itself.
171	
172	`printf 'man king woman\n' | timeout 2 /workspace/executable analogies sg.bin 3 | head`:
173	
174	```
175	Loading model sg.bin
176	Query triplet (A - B + C)? dog 0.997125
177	banana 0.996203
178	house 0.99608
179	Query triplet (A - B + C)? dog 0.997125   <- repeated forever after EOF
180	...
181	```
182	
183	## Summary of exit codes
184	
185	| situation | exit |
186	|---|---|
187	| successful query command (`print-*`, `nn` at EOF) | 0 |
188	| wrong argument count (usage, stdout) | 1 |
189	| model file missing / bad k (`stoi`, `k needs to be 1 or higher!`) | 134 (SIGABRT) |
190	| training with explicit `-maxn 0` | 134 (`Encountered NaN.`) |
191	| `analogies` at EOF | never exits (infinite loop) |

1	# Topic 06 — Quantization (`quantize`) — behavioral notes
2	
3	Binary: `/workspace/executable` (fastText-like). All runs from `/tmp/probe-quant`.
4	Training data: 600-line, 3-class corpus (`train.txt`), 60-line `valid.txt` (both generated with `random.seed(42)`).
5	
6	Models used:
7	- `supb.bin` — `supervised -input train.txt -output supb -thread 12 -dim 8 -minn 2 -maxn 5 -bucket 512` (46 words + 3 labels; input matrix 558×8; 18868 bytes)
8	- `sup.bin` — same but no subwords (input matrix 46×8; 2484 bytes)
9	- `sg.bin` — `skipgram -input train.txt -output sg -thread 1 -dim 8 -minCount 1 -minn 2 -maxn 5` (input matrix 2000046×8; 64003860 bytes)
10	- `ml.bin` — 300-label corpus `many.txt`, `supervised -dim 8 -thread 12 -epoch 3` (input 1793×8, output 300×8)
11	
12	## 1. Basic `quantize -output X`
13	
14	- Loads `<output>.bin` (NOT `-input`); writes `<output>.ftz`; **never modifies or re-saves the `.bin`** (md5 identical before/after).
15	- **Produces zero console output on success** (stdout and stderr both empty), at any `-verbose` level (tested 0, 1, 2). Exit code 0.
16	- Overwrites an existing `.ftz` silently.
17	- `-input` is not even opened unless `-retrain` is used: `quantize -input nosuch.txt -output supb` succeeds silently (exit 0).
18	- The input matrix must have **≥ 256 rows** or the process aborts:
19	  ```
20	  terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
21	    what():  Matrix too small for quantization, must have at least 256 rows
22	  ```
23	  (stderr, exit **134** = SIGABRT; no `.ftz` written, pre-existing `.ftz` left untouched).
24	  Triggered by: `sup.bin` (46 rows), and by any `-cutoff` < 256 (pruned matrix too small).
25	  Boundary verified: 255 rows → abort; 256 rows → OK.
26	- Fully deterministic: three identical runs give identical `.ftz` md5 (k-means seeded deterministically).
27	
28	## 2. `.ftz` file format vs `.bin`
29	
30	Identical 4-byte magic `ba 16 4f 2f` (0x2f4f16ba = 793712314) and version `0c 00 00 00` (12) for both.
31	Args section (12×int32: dim, ws, epoch, minCount, neg, wordNgrams, loss, model, bucket, minn, maxn, lrUpdateRate + double t) and dictionary section are **byte-identical** between `.bin` and `.ftz` (first diff at the quant flag, offset 882 in `supb`).
32	
33	Dictionary: `size i32, nwords i32, nlabels i32, ntokens i64, pruneidx_size i64`, then per entry `word\0 count:i64 type:u8`. If pruned (cutoff), `pruneidx_size > 0` and `pruneidx_size` pairs of `(oldId:i32, newId:i32)` follow the words.
34	
35	After the dictionary:
36	- `.bin`: `quant flag u8 = 0`, then dense input matrix `rows i64, cols i64, rows*cols f32`, then `qout flag u8 = 0`, then dense output matrix same layout.
37	- `.ftz`: `quant flag u8 = 1`, then a **QuantMatrix** for the input, then `qout flag u8`, then either a dense output matrix (qout=0) or a second QuantMatrix (qout=1).
38	
39	QuantMatrix layout (verified byte-exact for several files):
40	```
41	qnorm      u8
42	m          i64        # rows
43	n          i64        # cols (= dim)
44	codesSize  i32        # = m * nsubq   (NOTE: int32 byte count, no dsub here)
45	codes      u8[codesSize]
46	PQ header  4 x i32:   dim, nsubq, dsub, lastdsub
47	centroids  f32[256 * n]   # ksub=256, per-dim codebook
48	if qnorm:
49	  norm codes   u8[m]          # NO size prefix (asymmetric with codes above)
50	  norm PQ hdr  4 x i32: 1, 1, 1, 1
51	  norm centroids f32[256]
52	```
53	Size accounting checks out exactly (e.g. qnorm file: 883 + 1+8+8+4 + 2232 + 16 + 8192 + 558 + 16 + 1024 + 1 + 16 + 96 = 13055 = file size).
54	Note vs upstream fastText: this build stores an explicit `codesSize` int32 and a 4×i32 PQ header `(dim, nsubq, dsub, lastdsub)`; dsub is not stored as a separate int64.
55	
56	With `-qout`, the output matrix uses the identical QuantMatrix layout (e.g. qout flag=1, then `qnorm u8, m=299, n=8, codesSize=1196, codes, PQ(8,4,2,2), centroids`). `-qnorm` applies to the output QuantMatrix too (both get qnorm=1).
57	
58	## 3. Options
59	
60	Flags are pure switches — they take NO value. `quantize ... -qnorm true` →
61	`Provided argument without a dash! Usage:` + full usage dump, exit 1.
62	(The usage dump prints *current* parsed values: after `-qnorm` was consumed the dump shows `-qnorm ... [true]` whereas a fresh dump shows `[false]`.)
63	
64	- `-qnorm`: adds norm-codes (m bytes) + norm codebook (256 f32) with PQ header `(1,1,1,1)`. Also changes the main codes/centroids (vectors are normalized before quantization) — whole file differs from non-qnorm run.
65	- `-qout`: quantizes the output/classifier matrix. On the 3-label model it aborts with the same `Matrix too small for quantization, must have at least 256 rows` (exit 134). Works with 300 labels.
66	- `-dsub` (default 2):
67	  - `-dsub 3` with dim 8 (3 ∤ 8): **works**, exit 0. PQ header `(8, 3, 3, 2)` — lastdsub = 2.
68	  - `-dsub 4`: PQ header `(8, 2, 4, 4)`.
69	  - `-dsub 16` (> dim): **works**. codesSize = m*1, PQ header `(8, 1, 16, 8)` — dsub stored as given, nsubq=1, lastdsub=dim.
70	  - `-dsub 0`: **SIGFPE, exit 136, no message at all** (division by zero).
71	  - `-dsub -2`: `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::length_error'` / `what():  vector::_M_default_append`, exit 134.
72	- `-cutoff N`: keeps N total rows (top words + top ngram buckets). Dictionary is pruned (labels always kept) and a `pruneidx` map `(oldId,newId)` i32 pairs is written (`pruneidx_size = N - keptWords`; e.g. cutoff 256 → 23 words + 3 labels kept, pruneidx_size 233, matrix 256 rows).
73	  - N > total rows (e.g. 100000 > 558): no-op — output `.ftz` **byte-identical** to no-cutoff (md5 `10c2eeb9...`).
74	  - N = 0 or negative (e.g. -5): treated as disabled, byte-identical to default.
75	  - 0 < N < 256: aborts "Matrix too small..." (pruned matrix below 256 rows).
76	- `-retrain` (only meaningful with `-cutoff`; without cutoff it is a silent no-op, output byte-identical to default):
77	  - Retrains embeddings after pruning. Prints ONLY a progress line to **stderr**, no `Read 0M words` line (unlike training). Exact bytes (via `| cat -A`):
78	    ```
79	    ^MProgress: 100.0% words/sec/thread:   40815 lr: -0.000012 avg.loss:  0.777867 ETA:   0h 0m 0s^MProgress: 100.0% words/sec/thread:   40748 lr:  0.000000 avg.loss:  0.777867 ETA:   0h 0m 0s$
80	    ```
81	    (Note the transient negative lr `-0.000012` and the >100% progress overshoot — same cosmetic quirk as training, which also prints e.g. `Progress: 100.3% ... lr: -0.000316`.)
82	  - `-epoch` / `-lr` are honored during retrain: `-epoch 10 -lr 0.5` → avg.loss 0.063276 vs 0.777867 with defaults (epoch 5, lr 0.05).
83	
84	## 4. Quantizing a skipgram (unsupervised) model
85	
86	Always aborts, regardless of extra flags (`-qout`, `-cutoff` make no difference):
87	```
88	terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
89	  what():  For now we only support quantization of supervised models
90	```
91	exit 134, no `.ftz` written. So quantization is supervised-only in this build.
92	
93	## 5. Using the `.ftz`
94	
95	`test`, `test-label`, `predict`, `predict-prob`, `nn`, `analogies`, `print-word-vectors`, `print-sentence-vectors`, `print-ngrams`, `dump` all accept the `.ftz` path directly. `analogies` prints `Loading model supb.ftz` then `Query triplet (A - B + C)? `.
96	
97	- Predictions differ slightly from `.bin` (quantization error), e.g.:
98	  ```
99	  .bin: __label__sport 0.345966 __label__tech 0.328106
100	  .ftz: __label__sport 0.345964 __label__tech 0.328145
101	  ```
102	- `print-word-vectors` works, values close to but not equal to `.bin`.
103	- `test`/`test-label` output format identical to `.bin` runs.
104	- Pruned (cutoff) model still returns vectors for pruned-away words (subword fallback via pruneidx remap).
105	- `dump args` and `dump dict` work on `.ftz` (same format as `.bin`).
106	- `dump input` / `dump output` on `.ftz`: print `Not supported for quantized models.` to **stderr**, exit code **0** (no stdout).
107	
108	### QUIRK: `print-ngrams` prints uninitialized garbage (also on plain `.bin`!)
109	`print-ngrams supb.bin team` (and `.ftz`) emits absurd values — `-nan`, `-9.4576e+23`, `1.9927e+08` — for *some* vector components while others are sane. **Non-deterministic**: two identical runs differ (md5 mismatch); garbage positions/values vary per line and per run (e.g. one run: `<t 6.0779e+35 0.068016 6.0779e+35 ...` where columns 0 and 2 share the same garbage). Looks like reading uninitialized memory in the ngram-vector buffer. Exit code 0 regardless. `print-word-vectors`, `nn`, `predict` are NOT affected.
110	
111	## 6. Error cases summary
112	
113	| Case | Behavior | Exit |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| missing `<output>.bin` | `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'` / `what():  nosuch.bin cannot be opened for loading!` | 134 |
116	| missing `-output` (or `-input` value empty) | `Empty input or output path.` + usage | 1 |
117	| bare `quantize` (no args) | full usage text | 1 |
118	| missing `-input` file, no `-retrain` | silently ignored, quantizes fine | 0 |
119	| **missing `-input` file WITH `-retrain -cutoff`** | **HANGS FOREVER** — no output, no file, killed by timeout (>60 s; also with `-thread 1`) | — |
120	| input matrix < 256 rows | `std::invalid_argument`: `Matrix too small for quantization, must have at least 256 rows` | 134 |
121	| `-qout` with < 256 labels | same "Matrix too small" abort (output matrix) | 134 |
122	| quantize skipgram/cbow model | `std::invalid_argument`: `For now we only support quantization of supervised models` | 134 |
123	| `-dsub 0` | SIGFPE, no message | 136 |
124	| `-dsub < 0` | `std::length_error`: `vector::_M_default_append` | 134 |
125	| quantize an already-quantized file (`cp X.ftz Y.bin; quantize -output Y`) | **SIGSEGV, no message** | 139 |
126	| flag given a value (`-qnorm true`) | `Provided argument without a dash! Usage:` + usage | 1 |
127	
128	All `terminate called ...` messages go to stderr (two lines, each `\n`-terminated).
129	
130	## 7. Other observations
131	
132	- Quantize success is 100% silent — the only way to confirm is the `.ftz` file appearing.
133	- Deterministic for fixed args/model (identical md5 across runs), including `-cutoff`.
134	- `.ftz` is smaller than `.bin` here mostly because dense f32 rows (32 B/row at dim 8) become 4 code bytes/row + one shared 8 KB codebook (e.g. 18868 → 11457 bytes).
135	- The supervised training run itself prints the >100% progress / negative-lr cosmetic quirk (`Progress: 101.0% ... lr: -0.000977` then a corrected final `Progress: 100.0% ... lr:  0.000000`), also seen in quantize-retrain output.

10	- `sg.bin`: `skipgram -input sg.txt -output sg -thread 1 -dim 4 -minCount 1 -minn 2 -maxn 4 -epoch 5`
11	  (sg.txt: 8-line corpus repeated 20x; 28 word types incl. `</s>`).
12	- `supng.bin`: `supervised ... -thread 1 -dim 4 -wordNgrams 2` (bucket 2000000), then
13	  `quantize -input sup.txt -output supng -epoch 1` → `supng.ftz`.
14	- `cb.bin`: `cbow ... -thread 1 -dim 4 -minCount 1 -epoch 3 -loss hs -t 1e-5 -lr 0.777`.
15	
16	⚠ Training quirk (off-topic but blocking): `supervised` on this data with `-thread` ≤ 6
17	aborts with `fasttext::DenseMatrix::EncounteredNaNError` / `what():  Encountered NaN.`
18	(exit 134, core dump). `-thread 8` or `12` trains fine. Persists with 10x data and any
19	epoch/lr tested. skipgram/cbow with `-thread 1` are fine. Use `-thread 12` for supervised.
20	
21	## 1. Usage / errors
22	
23	`dump` with wrong arg count, missing option, or an invalid option (case-sensitive, e.g. `Dict`,
24	`bogus`) prints this to **stdout** and exits **1**:
25	
26	```
27	usage: fasttext dump <model> <option>
28	
29	  <model>      model filename
30	  <option>     option from args,dict,input,output
31	```
32	
33	(Exact bytes verified with `od -c`: text ends with `output\n`, single `\n\n` after the first
34	line, two-space indent before `<model>`/`<option>`.)
35	
36	Extra trailing args after the option are silently ignored (`dump sup.bin args extra` works).
37	
38	Model-loading failures abort (uncaught exception → SIGABRT, **exit 134**, message on stderr):
39	
40	- Nonexistent file: `what():  nonexistent.bin cannot be opened for loading!`
41	  (`std::invalid_argument`)
42	- Wrong magic (a `.vec` file, an empty file, or a directory): `what():  X has wrong file format!`
43	
44	## 2. `dump <model> args`
45	
46	Exact output for `sup.bin` (`| cat -A`, `$` = newline):
47	
48	```
49	dim 4$
50	ws 5$
51	epoch 5$
52	minCount 1$
53	neg 5$
54	wordNgrams 1$
55	loss softmax$
56	model sup$
57	bucket 0$
58	minn 0$
59	maxn 0$
60	lrUpdateRate 100$
61	t 0.0001$
62	```
63	
64	For `sg.bin` (`-minn 2 -maxn 4`): identical except `loss ns`, `model sg`, `bucket 2000000`,
65	`minn 2`, `maxn 4`.
66	
67	For `cb.bin` (`-loss hs -t 1e-5 -lr 0.777`): `epoch 3`, `loss hs`, `model cbow`,
68	`bucket 2000000`, `minn 3`, `maxn 6` (cbow defaults), `t 1e-05`.
69	
70	Fields, in fixed order (13 lines, space-separated `name value`, `\n`-terminated):
71	`dim ws epoch minCount neg wordNgrams loss model bucket minn maxn lrUpdateRate t`
72	
73	- **NOT dumped**: `lr`, `thread`, `input`, `output`, `verbose`, `seed`, etc. (`-lr 0.777`
74	  leaves no trace).
75	- Enums as lowercase names: `loss` ∈ {`softmax`, `ns`, `hs`, ...}, `model` ∈ {`sup`, `sg`, `cbow`}.
76	- Float formatting is C++ `std::cout` default (printf `%g`-like, 6 significant digits,
77	  trailing zeros stripped, scientific when small): `t 0.0001`, `t 1e-05` (two-digit exponent).
78	- Quirk: supervised default shows `bucket 0` (since sup has no subwords/ngrams by default),
79	  while sg/cbow show `bucket 2000000`. With `-wordNgrams 2` supervised shows `bucket 2000000`.
80	- Works identically on `.ftz` (quantized) models.
81	
82	## 3. `dump <model> dict`
83	
84	Format: first line = total entry count (nwords + nlabels), then one line per entry:
85	`<word> <count> <type>` (single spaces, `\n`-terminated), type ∈ {`word`, `label`}.
86	
87	Exact output for `sup.bin`:
88	
89	```
90	12
91	</s> 400 word
92	cat 246 word
93	banana 240 word
94	fish 238 word
95	hat 233 word
96	grape 224 word
97	dog 217 word
98	cherry 213 word
99	apple 203 word
100	__label__fruit 205 label
101	__label__animal 144 label
102	__label__other 51 label
103	```
104	
105	- Ordering: all `word` entries first (sorted by count descending), then all `label` entries
106	  (count descending). Words sort before labels even when a label has a higher count
107	  (`__label__fruit 205` > `apple 203` still comes after all words).
108	- Ties are not alphabetical: in sg.bin, count-20 words appear in an order matching neither
109	  alphabet nor first-appearance (hash-table/unstable-sort order), e.g.
110	  `together, play, mat, on, sat, animals, friends, are, run, day, all, sleeps, fast, runs, a, at, barks, over, jumps`.
111	  Order **is deterministic** across runs (verified with diff).
112	- Labels ARE included (`__label__*` lines). Subword ngrams are NOT listed.
113	- Counts are plain integers. Works on `.ftz` too (same output).
114	
115	## 4. `dump <model> input` / `output`
116	
117	Header line: `<rows> <dim>` then one row per line, values space-separated, **no trailing
118	space**, `\n` after each row. Floats in `std::cout` default format (6 sig figs, `%g`-like):
119	e.g. `0.0786222`, `0.00596287`, `1.15381` (trailing zero stripped), `0.000242869`.
120	
121	`sup.bin input`:
122	
123	```
124	9 4
125	-0.725893 0.41974 -0.324874 -0.403682
126	-0.236537 -0.390108 -0.70355 0.151414
127	... (9 rows total)
128	```
129	
130	- Input rows = **words only, in dict order** (labels excluded). Verified: row 2 = `cat`,
131	  row 9 = `apple`, matching `print-word-vectors` values.
132	- `sg.bin input`: header `2000028 4` = 28 words + 2000000 ngram buckets; word rows first
133	  (dict order), then bucket rows 0..1999999.
134	- `supng.bin` (supervised `-wordNgrams 2`) input: header `2000009 4` — **yes, ngram bucket
135	  rows are included** for supervised word-ngrams (row 11 onward are nonzero bucket vectors).
136	- `sup.bin output`: header `3 4` — 3 rows = the 3 labels (dict label order).
137	- `sg.bin`/`cb.bin` output: `28 4` — one row per word.
138	- Output is byte-identical across runs (deterministic).
139	
140	## 5. Quantized `.ftz` models
141	
142	- `dump supng.ftz args` → works, same text as the `.bin` (shows `wordNgrams 2`, `bucket 2000000`).
143	- `dump supng.ftz dict` → works, identical to `.bin`.
144	- `dump supng.ftz input` / `output` → **exit code 0**, empty stdout, and on **stderr** exactly:
145	
146	```
147	Not supported for quantized models.
148	```
149	
150	(with trailing `\n`, verified via `od -c`). I.e. failure is silently "successful" — only the
151	stderr message distinguishes it.
152	
153	Quantize constraints discovered while making the ftz: quantize refuses non-supervised models
154	(`For now we only support quantization of supervised models`) and tiny matrices
155	(`Matrix too small for quantization, must have at least 256 rows`) — a supervised model with
156	9 input rows can't be quantized without `-wordNgrams 2`/large `-bucket`.
157	
158	## 6. Summary of quirks
159	
160	1. Invalid dump option → usage on **stdout**, exit 1 (not an error message).
161	2. Missing/corrupt model file → abort with uncaught exception, exit 134.
162	3. `dump input/output` on `.ftz` → exit 0 with `Not supported for quantized models.` on stderr.
163	4. `dump args` omits `lr` entirely; floats are `%g`-style (`t 1e-05`).
164	5. Supervised default args dump shows `bucket 0` (sg/cbow show 2000000).
165	6. Dict ties are in hash-table order, not alphabetical — but deterministic.
166	7. (Training, off-topic) `supervised` + `-thread` ≤ 6 on small data → `Encountered NaN.` abort.
167	8. Extra arguments after a valid dump command are ignored.

1	# Topic 08 — Autotune (`-autotune-*`)
2	
3	Binary: `/workspace/executable` (fastText-like). All runs from `/tmp/probe-auto`.
4	All autotune console output goes to **stderr**; stdout is always empty. Exit 0 on success.
5	
6	## Test data
7	
8	Synthetic supervised data, python3-generated (seed 42), 3 labels `__label__pos/neg/neu`,
9	500 train lines (`train.txt`), 100 validation lines (`valid.txt`), 54 distinct words, `empty.txt` = 0 bytes.
10	
11	## Activation & basic behavior
12	
13	- Autotune activates **only** when `-autotune-validation <file>` is given.
14	  `-autotune-duration 3` alone (no validation file) silently runs **normal training** (exit 0, no autotune log).
15	- Command used: `/workspace/executable supervised -input ../train.txt -output m -autotune-validation ../valid.txt -autotune-duration 5 -thread 4`
16	- Output files: `m.bin` + `m.vec` (normal autotune); `m.ftz` + `m.vec` (no `.bin`!) when `-autotune-modelsize` is set.
17	- The tuned hyperparameters are **never printed to console**. After the run, `dump m.bin args` reveals them, e.g.:
18	  ```
19	  dim 177
20	  ws 5
21	  epoch 15
22	  minCount 1
23	  neg 5
24	  wordNgrams 5
25	  loss softmax
26	  model sup
27	  bucket 1193037
28	  minn 3
29	  maxn 6
30	  lrUpdateRate 100
31	  t 0.0001
32	  ```
33	  (no `lr`, `thread`, `dsub`, `cutoff` lines — fixed 14-line set). Sampled ranges observed:
34	  dim {169, 177, 42...}, epoch {15, 96...}, bucket {525506, 1193037, ~4.1M}, minn 3 / maxn 6 often on, wordNgrams up to 5.
35	- Trial search is **nondeterministic across identical runs** (trial counts/scores at the same progress marks differ between two `-autotune-duration 4` runs; diff confirmed). ~10–19 trials in 3–10 s on this tiny data.
36	- One run (duration 5) produced a **2.7 GB `m.bin`** (dim 169, bucket ≈ 4.1M) — autotune with no modelsize constraint happily picks huge buckets.
37	
38	## Exact console output (stderr, `cat -A`)
39	
40	Trial progress line — carriage-return-separated updates, no newline until the loop ends:
41	
42	```
43	^MProgress:  10.0% Trials:    2 Best score:  0.830000 ETA:   0h 0m 4s^MProgress:  20.0% Trials:    5 Best score:  0.830000 ETA:   0h 0m 3s ... ^MProgress: 100.0% Trials:   11 Best score:  1.000000 ETA:   0h 0m 0s$
44	Training again with best arguments$
45	^MRead 0M words$
46	Number of words:  54$
47	Number of labels: 3$
48	^MProgress: 100.0% words/sec/thread:  647438 lr: -0.000097 avg.loss:  0.118193 ETA:   0h 0m 0s^MProgress: 100.0% words/sec/thread:  647119 lr:  0.000000 avg.loss:  0.118193$
49	```
50	
51	- Progress update cadence: one update every **0.5 s** → number of updates = 2 × duration.
52	  Observed step sizes: duration 1 → 50.0% steps; 3 → 16.7% (last shown 83.4%, not 83.3); 4 → 12.5%; 5 → 10.0%; 10 → 5.0%.
53	- Field widths: `Progress: %5.1f%`, `Trials: %4d` (space-padded), `Best score: %9s`-ish — note two spaces before `0.830000`.
54	  When no qualifying trial yet (modelsize constraint): `Best score:   unknown` (3 spaces). Empty validation: `Best score:       nan`.
55	- ETA format `ETA: %3dh %dm %ds` e.g. `ETA:   0h 0m 4s`.
56	- After the last progress update a single `\n` is emitted, then the literal line `Training again with best arguments\n`, then a normal training log (with `\rRead 0M words`, `Number of words:  54` — two spaces after colon, `Number of labels: 3` — one space).
57	- `-verbose 0` does **not** suppress the autotune progress lines.
58	
59	## `-autotune-duration`
60	
61	- Default per usage text: `[300]`.
62	- `0` or negative (e.g. `-5`): aborts, exit 134 (SIGABRT, uncaught C++ exception), a 0-byte `m.bin` is left behind:
63	  ```
64	  terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
65	    what():  Didn't have enough time to train once: please increase `autotune-duration`.
66	  ```
67	
68	## `-autotune-metric`
69	
70	- `f1` (default) works.
71	- `f1:labelname` requires the **full label including the `-label` prefix**: `f1:__label__pos` works
72	  (per-label F1, e.g. `Best score:  0.857143`); bare `f1:pos` **aborts** exit 134:
73	  ```
74	  terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
75	    what():  Unknown autotune metric label
76	  ```
77	  Same message for a nonexistent full label (`f1:__label__nope`).
78	- Unknown metric name (`foo`): exit 134, `std::runtime_error`, `what():  Unknown metric : foo` (space before colon).
79	- `-autotune-predictions 2` works (changes scores, e.g. 0.553333/0.666667 — F1@2-style metric).
80	
81	## `-autotune-modelsize`
82	
83	- `100k` works: output is `m.ftz` (97629 bytes) + small `m.vec` (no `m.bin`). `.ftz` magic = `ba 16 4f 2f` (0x2f4f16ba) + version 12.
84	  - Early trials whose size exceeds the constraint log `Best score:   unknown`.
85	  - Mid-run (between two `^M` progress updates, on its own `^M`-terminated line) this warning appeared at 60%:
86	    ```
87	    Warning : requested model size is probably too small. You may want to increase `autotune-modelsize`.
88	    ```
89	    (note the space before the colon: `Warning :`).
90	  - After "Training again with best arguments" there are **two** training progress sequences (final train, then quantization retrain).
91	  - Quantized artifacts are aggressively pruned: `m.vec` header was `5 42` — only 5 rows retained
92	    (`</s>`, `great`, `ugly`, `terrible`, `sad`), dim 42. `test m.ftz valid.txt` → `N 100 / P@1 0.73 / R@1 0.73`.
93	- `2M` works: `m.ftz` 1,939,330 bytes, full-size `m.vec` (50293 bytes), **no** warning.
94	- Unparsable size (`abc`): exit 134, `std::invalid_argument`, `what():  Unable to parse model size abc`.
95	
96	## Error cases (all exit 134 = SIGABRT via uncaught exception, message on stderr)
97	
98	- Missing validation file:
99	  ```
100	  terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
101	    what():  Validation file cannot be opened!
102	  ```
103	- **Empty validation file**: NO error — every trial logs `Best score:       nan`, then it retrains
104	  "with best arguments" (effectively default-ish args, avg.loss 1.049423 ≈ default lr 0.1 run) and exits 0,
105	  producing a valid `m.bin`/`m.vec`.
106	- Autotune with `skipgram` or `cbow`: exit 134,
107	  ```
108	  terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
109	    what():  Model needs to be supervised for prediction!
110	  ```
111	  (0-byte `m.bin` left behind.) → autotune is supervised-only.
112	- Missing training input: exit 134, `std::invalid_argument`, `what():  ../missing.txt cannot be opened for training!`
113	
114	## NaN abort quirk (intermittent)
115	
116	- Claim "thread < 10 always NaNs in supervised training" did **not** reproduce in plain training on this data:
117	  `-thread 4/9/10/11/12`, `-lr` up to 5.0, `-epoch` up to 50, `-minn 3 -maxn 6 -wordNgrams 5 -dim 177` all exited 0.
118	- However, the **final retrain after autotune crashed with NaN in 2 of ~8 autotune runs** (both with `-thread 4`;
119	  durations 10 and 3, the latter also `-verbose 0`). Symptom — after `Training again with best arguments`:
120	  ```
121	  ^MProgress:   0.0% words/sec/thread:       0 lr:  0.319578 avg.loss:  6.515641 ETA: 720h 0m 0sterminate called after throwing an instance of 'fasttext::DenseMatrix::EncounteredNaNError'
122	    what():  Encountered NaN.
123	  ```
124	  Exit 134, 0-byte `m.bin` left behind. Note the exception line is appended directly after the `\r` progress
125	  fragment with no newline, and the absurd `ETA: 720h 0m 0s` (720 h exactly) appears whenever the first
126	  progress tick fires with 0 words/sec.
127	- A repeat of the identical duration-10 command succeeded — so the abort is **nondeterministic**
128	  (depends on which hyperparameters win the race + thread interleaving), not a fixed thread<10 rule.
129	- Autotune **trials themselves never crashed** with NaN in any run; only the final retrain did.
130	
131	## Misc
132	
133	- `-autotune-duration 10 -thread 4`: 19 trials in 10 s; best score reached 1.000000 quickly on this separable data.
134	- Usage text (bare `supervised`) lists autotune options exactly as:
135	  ```
136	  The following arguments are for autotune:
137	    -autotune-validation            validation file to be used for evaluation
138	    -autotune-metric                metric objective {f1, f1:labelname} [f1]
139	    -autotune-predictions           number of predictions used for evaluation  [1]
140	    -autotune-duration              maximum duration in seconds [300]
141	    -autotune-modelsize             constraint model file size [] (empty = do not quantize)
142	  ```
143	  (note double space before `[1]` on the predictions line).
